articleSummary: Phytobacter diazotrophicus, an emergent bacterium, triggered a neonatal sepsis outbreak in Brazil from October 2013 to May 2014, affecting 65 newborns across Paraná, Minas Gerais, São Paulo and Rio Grande do Sul and causing 15 deaths. articleSummary: Thailand aims to end tuberculosis (TB) by 2035, aligning with SDG targets. Globally, TB causes about 1.38 million deaths annually (≈3,400 daily) and roughly 10.7 million new cases; Thailand reports about 104,000 new cases and 11,300 deaths per year. Progress hinges on proactive, AI- and molecular-diagnostic–driven case finding, universal health coverage supporting affordable care, and integrated services across districts to sustain high cure rates. The four-pronged plan emphasizes: accelerate detection with AI and molecular tech; scale up safe, short-course TB treatment; integrate TB care with social protection; and back research and innovation under the slogan “Know Early, Cure, Don’t Spread, No Stigma.” WHO Thailand commends leadership, rapid molecular diagnostics, and expanded MDR-TB treatment, with support for migrant workers and urban populations to ensure no one is left behind. Citizens with a cough lasting more than two weeks are advised to seek free chest X-ray and sputum testing.
notes: 結核は世界的な風土病であり、タイによる新たな目標達成計画（2035年までの結核停止）は重要な政策展開だが、急性的な新規感染症危機やアウトブレイク事象ではない。WHOとの協力強化、AI・分子診断の活用、薬剤耐性結核の治療拡大など進展的取組みが報告されており、感染症イベントとしてはPICKUPの基準を満たさないが、タイの結核対策の動向把握として注視する価値がある。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Urgent need to enhance the prevention and control of drug-resistant tuberculosis.
articleHeadline: 亟待提升耐药结核病防治水平
articleSummary: DR-TB, especially rifampicin-resistant TB, remains a major TB-control challenge due to high transmission, long regimens and costly therapy. In China, second-line treatment lasts 18–24 months with complex regimens and notable adverse effects, and cure rates are only about 50–75%. Incomplete treatment accelerates transmission of resistant strains. Payment gaps under DRG/DIP bundle DR-TB with ordinary TB, leaving high inpatient costs undercompensated and pressuring facilities to skimp on essential, expensive drugs. Although bedaquiline, delamanid, and pretomanid are on the urban–rural resident insurance list (category B), self-pay still ranges from 50% to 70%, with total full-course costs around 200,000 CNY and out-of-pocket near 100,000 CNY. Proposals: establish a dedicated DR-TB fund to provide free second-line drugs; implement a ‘insurance reimbursement with government backing’ model to achieve zero self-pay; reclassify key drugs to category A; strengthen cross-department social support and emergency assistance to reduce patient burden.
notes: 記事は耐薬結核の既知の課題（治療コスト、低い治癒率、不完全な治療による耐性株の伝播）を中心に、中国の医療政策改善を提言する論説的性格が強い。新規クラスター、異常な流行拡大、または緊急対応要請の具体的な報告ではなく、むしろシステム的な課題提起である。WPROスクリーニング基準では複数該当するが、IHR基準は限定的（深刻度のみ）であり、国際的拡大のリスク記述もない。続報で具体的な流行事象が報告されれば、PICKUPに格上げする可能性あり。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Promising drug identified against Hepatitis E.
articleHeadline: Vielversprechender Wirkstoff gegen Hepatitis E identifiziert
articleSummary: Bemnifosbuvir identified as a potential treatment against Hepatitis E Virus (HEV). An international team from Ruhr-Universität Bochum, Heidelberg University Hospital's CIID and Peking University screened about 500 nucleotide/nucleoside analogues from a commercial library to block HEV replication. Using a reporter HEV in cell cultures, Bemnifosbuvir halted viral replication while preserving cell health; in vivo studies in China confirmed reduced HEV activity and liver inflammation. The findings, reported in Gut on March 6, 2026, suggest that if ongoing clinical trials of Bemnifosbuvir for Hepatitis C succeed, off-label use against HEV could be feasible soon. HEV is a leading cause of acute viral hepatitis; around 70,000 deaths annually; infections can become chronic in immunocompromised patients and are particularly dangerous in pregnancy. Currently no vaccine or approved specific therapy exists, highlighting the potential impact of this finding.
notes: 本イベントは新規感染症流行の報告ではなく、既知のHepatitis E に対する治療薬開発の科学的成果報告である。記事は臨床試験段階の進展を述べており、緊急的な公衆衛生危機を示唆していない。ただしドイツと中国の国際共同研究であり、HEV は年間7万人の死亡者を出す重要な感染症であるため、将来の治療導入時には注視の価値あり。現時点ではシグナルとして扱う基準を満たさない。

articleSummary: Measles, an RNA virus from the Paramyxoviridae family, remains a public health concern in Indonesia. 2025 data show 11,094 cases with 69 deaths; 2026 reports until present record 572 cases and 4 deaths. Incubation up to 14 days. Initial prodrome lasts 2–7 days: high fever, malaise, runny nose, cough, and photophobia; Koplik spots may appear inside the cheeks. A generalized rash develops between days 4–14, typically starting on the face or behind the ears and spreading to the body, with high fever. The rash often fades after 3–4 days and darkens to brownish tones, resolving over about 10 days. High-risk groups include infants, the immunocompromised, and those with malnutrition or vitamin A deficiency; pregnancy may cause miscarriage or preterm birth. Prevention hinges on MMR vaccination, given at 9 months, 2 years, and 5–6 years. Early healthcare seeking and limiting contact help prevent transmission.

articleSummary: Mutant Hyalomma ticks have appeared in southern Russia, acting as fast 'hunters' that chase humans rather than lying in grass. articleHeadline: Chennai: Guindy Children's Park closed after avian flu outbreak
articleSummary: Chennai's Guindy Children's Park has been closed after an avian influenza outbreak. Nearly 40 birds died at the facility since March 13, 2026. articleSummary: In the United Kingdom, an urgent outbreak of invasive meningococcal disease (Neisseria meningitidis, serogroup B) has prompted a national-level response. The disease spreads by droplets; incubation is 3–4 days and can deteriorate rapidly, with death possible within 24 hours of onset. Youths and young adults are most affected; two healthy individuals aged 18 and 21 have died, and a 9‑month‑old infant requires ICU care. Authorities call it unprecedentedly severe. Serogroup B is more dangerous than A, C, W, or Y, and many 15+ individuals remain unvaccinated since B vaccination was only added to routine schedules in 2015; dense teen gatherings facilitate transmission. As Easter holidays approach, UK travelers may return to Hong Kong, posing importation risk. For travelers, discuss targeted MenB vaccination with a GP; reinforce masks, hand hygiene, and prompt clinician consultation with travel history. Clinicians should screen travelers and use high‑dose antibiotics as needed.

articleSummary: Bahia state's Health Secretariat issued Portaria No. 240 on March 18, 2026, regulating access to public and private properties for health surveillance to combat arboviruses such as dengue, Zika, and chikungunya in Bahia, Brazil. Published in the State Official Gazette, the measure establishes formal procedures for interventions in risk situations, including abandoned properties, absence of residents, or access refusals. In residential properties, access is limited to exterior areas when residents are away or refuse without justification; in abandoned buildings, entry may be inside. The regulation requires incident recording, prior public notice, and authorization by the competent sanitary authority; enforcement may involve security forces. After each action, formal records and possible sanitary infraction notices are required. State Health Secretary Roberta Santana said the rule provides objective criteria and legal backing to strengthen vector control and rapid public health response.

articleSummary: Botulism poisoning linked to fermented fish (cá ủ chua) continues in Da Nang, Vietnam. As of 20 March 2026, two additional hospitalizations occurred on 18 and 20 March in Da Nang City, after consuming cá ủ chua in Phước Năng commune (thôn 3), with patients treated at Phước Sơn Regional Medical Center. This follows the 8 March incident in which three children in the same commune were critically ill; WHO arranged Botulism Antitoxin Heptavalent from Switzerland, administered around 11 March, with improving conditions. articleSummary: Antimicrobial resistance, fueling 'superbugs', is a rising concern in Ceará, Brazil. A The Lancet projection suggests deaths tied to antimicrobial resistance could rise nearly 70% by 2050, with significant impact in Latin America, South Asia, and the Caribbean, including Brazil. The initiative aims to reduce indiscriminate antibiotic use and help curb one of modern health care’s biggest challenges.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Felipeh Campos Case: Learn which medications to avoid when dengue is suspected.
articleHeadline: Caso Felipeh Campos: Saiba quais remédios evitar diante de suspeita de dengue
articleSummary: Felipeh Campos was hospitalized with dengue hemorrhagic fever, highlighting risks of self-medication in suspected dengue. An infectious disease specialist notes dengue can start mild but progress rapidly, and using anti-inflammatories without guidance may worsen bleeding by impairing platelet function and numbers. Medications formally contraindicated in dengue or suspected dengue include acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin), ibuprofen, diclofenac, nimesulide, cetoprofen, naproxen, and corticosteroids such as dexamethasone and prednisone. Safe options for pain and fever are dipyrone and paracetamol, though liver risk must be considered. Dengue often worsens on days 5–6, after fever subsides, with warning signs like severe abdominal pain, bleeding, persistent vomiting, and low blood pressure. Re-infection with a different dengue serotype increases severity due to heightened inflammatory response. Prevention remains essential; vaccination exists, but vector control at home accounts for about 80% of mosquito breeding sites.

Vaccination is advised for high-risk travelers and takes two weeks to become effective, so Easter travel plans should vaccinate promptly, alongside reinforced hygiene.

articleSummary: Dengue fever remains a public health concern in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, with adults increasingly affected. At the Hospital for Tropical Diseases in Ho Chi Minh City, a 34-year-old man illustrates dengue’s dangerous defervescence phase: fever subsides, yet shock risk rises as plasma leakage, hemoconcentration and thrombocytopenia progress to dengue shock syndrome, liver or kidney failure, or multiorgan injury. Severe cases have risen from about 15% to 17–19% in recent years. The disease appears year-round, with peaks June–October, driven by urbanization and climate change; Aedes mosquitoes breed in clean-water containers inside homes. Many patients delay care with at-home treatment, worsening outcomes. Families endure economic and social disruption, as illustrated by parents at BV Nhi Dong 1. Prevention highlights eliminating breeding sites, covering water storage, using nets and vector-control, and vaccination. Warning signs requiring urgent care include high fever, severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, and bleeding.

articleSummary: An 11-year-old girl in Phu Quoc, Vietnam, died of meningococcal meningitis, prompting rapid contact tracing, isolation of close contacts, and environmental cleaning to prevent spread. The disease begins with abrupt fever, headache, sore throat, and fatigue; severe cases may include neck stiffness, rash, or seizures, with infants showing irritability or poor feeding. Nasopharyngeal carriage is common (10–20%), and transmission occurs via respiratory droplets or contaminated surfaces, especially in schools or dormitories. Close contacts—household members, roommates, classmates, or caregivers—should receive prophylaxis and be monitored for 10 days; the exposure window spans seven days before to 24 hours after antibiotic initiation. Vietnam licenses five vaccines: MenQuadfi and Nimenrix for serogroups A, C, Y, W; Menactra for 9 months–55 years; Bexsero and VA-Mengoc-BC for group B. Vaccination should be early and in combination (B plus A/C/Y/W) since no cross-protection. Maintain hygiene, ventilation, and masking in public spaces.

articleSummary: Urinary tract infection (UTI) symptoms and prevention in Thailand: UTIs are commonly caused by Escherichia coli and can ascend from the bladder to the kidneys. Classic signs include frequent or painful urination, lower abdominal (suprapubic) fullness, and sometimes fever or chills if the infection spreads. Urine may be cloudy, strong-smelling, or pink/red if there is blood. Women are more susceptible due to a shorter urethra. Prevention emphasizes hydration, not delaying urination, postcoital urination, and proper genital hygiene; after bowel movements wipe front-to-back; avoid irritants and change menstrual pads regularly. Treatment is usually antibiotics, with improvement in 2–3 days; complete the full course to prevent resistance. Recurrent UTIs may warrant low-dose preventive therapy; probiotics may help reduce long-term risk. If symptoms persist or worsen, further evaluation is advised to prevent kidney involvement. Published 2026-03-21.
notes: 本記事はタイの保健情報サイトによる一般向けの教育記事であり、E. coli関連の尿路感染症アウトブレイクの報告ではない。既知疾患に関する予防啓発コンテンツとして、感染症危機管理の対象外。

articleSummary: On 21 March 2026, a 12-day-old newborn with varicella (chickenpox) complicated by pneumonia and severe respiratory failure was saved at Lao Cai Provincial Obstetrics and Pediatrics Hospital. The infant was admitted after 3 days of fever and a generalized vesicular rash with poor feeding; the condition rapidly progressed to respiratory failure and pneumonia. He required mechanical ventilation, antiviral therapy, antibiotics, intensive care, and nasogastric feeding. After 10 days of treatment, the baby began breathing spontaneously, fed well, skin lesions resolved, and overall health stabilized. Varicella-Zoster virus spreads via respiratory droplets and direct contact; in newborns, infection can lead to pneumonia, respiratory failure, hepatitis, and potentially death if not promptly treated. Experts advise pregnant women to limit contact with suspected cases, vaccination during pregnancy where appropriate, and families with newborns to monitor fever, rash, and feeding difficulties and seek early care. Preventive measures include hygiene, handwashing, isolation, and protecting high-risk individuals.

articleHeadline: Zimbabwe on high alert as foot-and-mouth disease threat grows
articleSummary: Zimbabwe remains on high alert for Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) amid a regional SADC threat, with a virulent Type O identified in Mozambique and Zambia. In Zimbabwe, infections are confined to ecological hotspots along wildlife corridors and near national parks, Four and Five. The Zambezi River provides a barrier to Zambia, but movement across the Mozambican border remains a higher risk. About 316,000 cattle across four districts are under FMD quarantine, excluding them from live animals and products trade. Suspected cases continue and are reported to the World Organisation for Animal Health after laboratory confirmations. Most confirmed outbreaks are in Mangwe District near Botswana; concerns about spread to districts like Bikita, Gokwe, and Gutu persist. Vaccine shortages hamper vaccination; new doses are expected from Botswana to resume campaigns around conservancies and parks. Containment measures include movement restrictions, roadblocks, fencing around Gonarezhou (extending to Hwange) and intensified biosecurity training.
